passage:
At noon, the playground had almost no shade. Students waited under a small roof, crowded together.
A geography teacher asked her class to study the problem. They watched how shadows moved during the day and drew a map of the playground.
The class suggested adding shade sails near the basketball court and planting trees along the fence. The principal used their report in a school meeting.
The shade sails were added before summer. The trees would take longer to grow, but students watered them every week.
The project showed students that geography was not only about maps in books. It could help solve a real problem under the hot sun.
